page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It features 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating with dedicated CPU allocation. The system includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 2.0 GB of RAM, offering 1.0 GB per vCPU. This instance includes no bundled GPUs and no local NVMe storage, relying on network-attached storage for persistent disk drives.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2d-highcpu-2 exhibits strong single-core compute capabilities, achieving a top 25% result in single-core CPU stress tests alongside average single-threaded compression performance. However, because the instance relies on a single physical core with hyper-threading across 2 vCPUs, multi-core and parallel scaling performance are constrained, scoring in the lower percentile ranges for multi-core stress tests, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is similarly limited due to the small memory footprint, with read and write throughput testing in the lower performance brackets.

The n2d-highcpu-2 provides a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight compute-bound workloads that prioritize single-thread processing over large memory footprints or parallel execution. Due to its constrained 2.0 GB memory capacity and lack of local ephemeral storage, it is not suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching, or parallel multi-threaded batch jobs. Optimal workloads include small single-threaded microservices, lightweight web utilities, background batch scripts, and simple CI/CD runner tasks requiring dedicated CPU resources.

The hardware topology features a 32 MB L3 cache, with no local SSD storage or integrated GPUs available. Benchmark metrics highlight strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top 25% for single-threaded stress testing, alongside average single-threaded decompression rates. Conversely, multi-core efficiency, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput are constrained by the single-core physical topology and modest memory size. The n2d-highcpu-2 represents an economical selection for single-threaded microservices, lightweight CI/CD tasks, simple background execution scripts, and utility services that benefit from dedicated processing cores without requiring high memory density or local storage.
